scope:
Compare attention arithmetic on identical pretrained first-block Q/K/V.

Isolated self/cross attention, not a whole-flow latency or quality claim. The
FP32 candidate promotes SDPA inputs/intermediates and restores the input dtype;
weights, masks and attention scale are unchanged. Native CPU BF16 and a CPU
precision diagnostic are both retained as references.
ir_observation: Stock SDPA QK scores, scale, softmax and AV are BF16. Promoted SDPA uses FP32 throughout and casts output back to BF16; its frontend decomposes into pre-scaling both Q and K before matmul. Both use HiFi4 and FP32 destination accumulation.
finding: Self-attention relative L2 falls 10.21% to 3.28%; cross-attention stays about 1.80%/1.90%. Native CPU BF16 differs only 0.085%/0.134% from the CPU precision diagnostic on these inputs. First-block arithmetic warrants investigation, but blanket SDPA promotion is not established as a quality fix.
limit: Synthetic learned first-block Q/K/V, isolated operator boundary with canonical contiguous inputs. Does not prove exact full-flow operator attribution, sampler quality, CUDA equivalence or end-to-end performance.
next: Test explicit FP32 QK matmul followed by scaling, avoiding promoted SDPA pre-scaling. Inspect scalar/softmax/matmul math on identical inputs before a full-flow change.
tests: 5 CPU checks cover original self/cross reconstruction with nonzero LoRA in FP32/BF16 and FP32-SDPA dtype restoration. Hardware outputs repeat bitwise and match the no-export control.
reproduce: python experiments/tenstorrent/attention_diagnostic.py --export-ir --output-dir /path/to/new; repeat without --export-ir in another process and compare fixtures/outputs bitwise.
